transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Carlos Gomez (Redwood SE); Lena Huang (Redwood CSM); Anita Rao (Veridian Head of MLOps); Tom Berger (Platform Eng); Sofia Lin (PM); Evan Cho (Security)

Summary (auto): Finalize plan for canary cutover and go-live. Decide on 10% initial traffic, A/B test for quality, monitoring hooks, and runbook ownership. Security and RBAC checks required pre-cutover.

[00:00] Maya: Okay everyone thanks for joining, we got a pretty tight agenda today — main focus is rollout plan, cutover and monitoring. quick check in from Veridian, any blockers?
[00:18] Anita: Yeah thanks Maya, nothing big right now. We've got the staging environment mirroring prod-ish, some small dataset privacy checks in flight but engineering is clear to run the smoke tests.
[00:30] Tom: one note, our platform team needs RBAC mapped before we give production traffic; we can do two service accounts for canary.
[00:40] Carlos: that's great, Tom. we'll make sure the runbook includes service account steps. quick question on traffic split — are we still on the 10% canary?
[00:52] Maya: proposal is 10% for first 48 hours, then 25% for a week, then full cutover if metrics look good. happy to adjust based on your risk tolerance.
[01:10] Sofia: For product success criteria, we want to make sure the quality delta is negligible. We'll run an A/B with control = existing model and treatment = Redwood inference. primary metric is mean NPS on sampled completions and a secondary metric latency p95.
[01:35] Evan: Security is green on SOC2 controls but we need KMS key policy review; can you share the KMS config docs?
[01:44] Maya: yes we'll share KMS integration guide and the SOC2 report link (https://redwood.docs/soc2) after the call.
[01:53] Anita: also please include audit log retention details. we have compliance that requires 1 year retention.
[02:05] Carlos: noted, audit logs retention default is 90 days on hosted but dedicated/private can be extended; i'll include options in the doc.

[02:30] Maya: let's walk through the canary cutover steps I pasted in the doc, step 1 staging verification, step 2 smoke tests, step 3 small traffic split, monitoring, rollback criteria, etc.
[02:45] Carlos: staging verification — we want a smoke test that covers MLP, latency under synthetic load, and KV cache warmup. i can run a 10 minute burst at 2x normal qps to ensure no perf cliffs.
[03:05] Tom: we'll give you access to the service accounts by tomorrow morning.
[03:12] Sofia: on A/B specifics: we'll route 10% traffic to Redwood variant and 90% to control for the first 48 hours; we'll sample 5k completions for quality eval and run statistical test, if p < 0.05 we'll pause.
[03:35] Maya: good, and we should define clear rollback triggers — failure rate > 1% or latency p95 increase > 50% over baseline or quality regression above threshold.
[03:50] Evan: can we get alerts in PagerDuty and also a slack channel? Security wants review of alert contents to avoid PII.
[04:02] Lena: we'll create a dedicated slack channel redwood-veridian-pilot and hook alerts there; PD escalation policy we'll align after runbook review.

[04:20] Carlos: about monitoring: we'll push dashboards for latency, error rate, token cost per request and quality drift. perf metrics come from the runtime, quality from sampled completions and evaluations — we'll include automatic diffs and regression alerts.
[04:40] Anita: token cost per request is huge for finance, can you include estimated unit costs for the projected load?
[04:50] Maya: yes, we'll share a cost estimate spreadsheet; it will include batching and quantization options to reduce unit costs.

[05:10] Tom: on the infra side, our infra-as-code will manage the routing rule, but we need the exact endpoint and API contract to do the cutover. can you give that?
[05:20] Carlos: the endpoint is the standard Redwood API with a canary route param; i'll send the exact curl examples and terraform snippet.
[05:30] Maya: i'll include the terraform sample in the runbook link.

[06:00] Sofia: for A/B analytics we will need event forwarding to our analytics pipeline — does Redwood support event hooks to Kinesis / PubSub?
[06:12] Carlos: yes we can forward logs and sampled completions to S3/Kinesis for you, or set up a webhook. will include config.

[06:40] Anita: timeline — ideally we want to start canary next week. any blockers preventing the 2026-07-24 staging smoke test?
[06:50] Tom: my team needs until Friday morning to hand over the service accounts, otherwise we're clear.
[07:03] Maya: sounds like we aim for staging smoke test Friday 2026-07-24 10:00 PT. i'll put calendar invite and include Carlos for the bench.

[07:20] Carlos: on bench — i'll run baseline throughput at peak QPS and run a cache warmup script; logging will be uploaded to the shared S3 bucket.
[07:32] Evan: on data residency, we need assurance that PHI won't be stored outside our region; is there a config for region pinning?
[07:42] Maya: yes we have region pinning for dedicated and private; for hosted we'll need to discuss regional availability. i'll flag this to the PM and ops.

[08:00] Anita: one last thing — our legal wants a short note about incident response SLA and escalation path.
[08:08] Lena: i can share the enterprise SLA summary and incident runbook.

[08:20] Maya: recapping action items — Maya to share runbook + dashboards; Carlos to run smoke test and bench and upload logs; Tom to provide RBAC and service accounts; Sofia to confirm A/B success criteria; Evan to review KMS doc.

[08:40] Sofia: and we'll define the quality evaluation script, i'll draft criteria and share it by Monday.

[09:00] Maya: any other concerns or hidden dependencies?
[09:05] Anita: none from my side. excited to move forward.
[09:10] Maya: great, we'll reconvene after the staging smoke test to decide go/no-go. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
